findings.claim: The central explanation repeatedly says a pipe sends a command's 'output' to the next command, without identifying standard output. In Bash, an ordinary | connects the first command's standard output to the next command's standard input; standard error is not included unless |& (or an explicit redirection) is used. Because the objective asks what a pipe passes, the current wording establishes an overbroad mental model and is repeated in the recap, cheat sheet, Markdown, and GIFT item.

evidence.section: Pipelines (standard output connected to standard input; |& connects standard error too)

findings.recommendation: Change the objective-facing explanation to 'a pipe sends standard output (stdout) to the next command's standard input (stdin)' and briefly note that errors on stderr are separate. Make the same correction in the recap, cheat sheet, artifact.md, and artifact.gift; do not redesign the simulator dispatch.

findings.claim: The source receipts for navigating-the-shell, pipes-and-grep, file-permissions, and environment-variables-and-secrets cite man7.org mirrors for GNU Bash, grep, coreutils ls/pwd/wc/chmod/env, while the repository contract requires live official first-party sources. The fetched mirror bytes are live and internally consistent, but the host is not the GNU project's first-party documentation host; equivalent current GNU manuals are available from gnu.org.
findings.recommendation: Replace the GNU-command mirror citations in all four affected sources.json files and learner disclosures with current gnu.org Bash, grep, and Coreutils manual URLs, live-fetch them, record retrieval timestamps and sha256 values, and retain the existing official POSIX, Git, GitHub, RFC Editor, and Linux-man-pages evidence where appropriate.

findings.claim: The page teaches the generic rule 'echo $NAME prints it' and repeats the unquoted form in the recap and cheat sheet. An unquoted parameter expansion is subject to word splitting (and then filename expansion), so it does not reliably preserve an arbitrary variable's value. The GIFT companion already models the safer echo "$REGION" form.

evidence.section: Word Splitting (results not within double quotes are split)

findings.recommendation: Teach and repeat echo "$NAME" (or printf '%s\n' "$NAME") when reading a variable. Keep the simulator's accepted command set if needed, but display the quoted form in teaching, recap, cheat sheet, Markdown, and completion guidance.

findings.claim: All five video.json receipts hash their current video-artifact.md bytes, but under the documented evidence-binding precedence they omit a target and therefore default to the topic artifact.html. The generated module lock consequently records all five video bindings as current: false even though T17 separately interprets the same hashes as video-artifact.md and passes. The committed evidence is internally inconsistent and does not provide a current lock binding to the files it actually reviewed.
findings.recommendation: Give each video.json receipt an explicit repo-relative reviewedPath naming its topic's video-artifact.md (or add an equivalent schema-supported target field), then regenerate module.lock.json and verify all five video evidence bindings resolve to video-artifact.md with current: true.
